title: My grandmother left me a voicemail from the hospital. She died two days before she called.
transcript:
My grandmother left me a voicemail from the hospital. She died two days before she called. The voicemail came in at 2:14 AM on a Thursday. I saw the name before I fell back asleep. Grandma. I felt a stupid flash of hope, and then I remembered the funeral had been on Tuesday.

I played it in the morning.

Her voice was small. "Honey, it's me. I'm still at the hospital. They keep moving my bed. Listen, a nurse comes at night. She has your mother's face. Don't let her in."

I deleted it. I'm not proud of that. I told myself it was a glitch.

The next night, at 2:14, another voicemail. Different message.

"Honey, she has your face now. Check your bathroom mirror."

I didn't check. I slept with the light on.

Friday at 2:14 there was a third one. This time my grandmother wasn't whispering, she was crying, fast and terrified.

"She's at your door. She knows you got the messages. Whatever you do, don't answer when she says it's me."

Then the call dropped.

I'm writing this from my kitchen. It's 2:13.

My phone is ringing, and it says Grandma.
